draft.title: Cooling-off periods
card: A cooling-off period is a short time after signing a contract in which the buyer can change their mind and cancel. The buyer does not need a reason.
Not every purchase has one. Some sales have a cooling-off period, such as those made by a door-to-door seller. Buying something in a shop usually does not.
The length of the period depends on the type of sale. It is often a matter of days, and the clock starts after the contract is signed.
The idea is to protect buyers from pressure. A seller at your door can make it hard to say no, so the buyer gets time to think it over.
draft.remember: A cooling-off period lets a buyer cancel some contracts within a few days, with no reason needed.

a.q: Which best describes a cooling-off period?
opts: Time after signing in which a buyer can cancel a contract
Time before signing in which a seller must hold a price
Time after buying in which a faulty product can be fixed
Time in which a buyer must pay the full price of a contract
a.why: A cooling-off period starts after the contract is signed and lets the buyer cancel without giving a reason. Time to fix a faulty product is a different idea, because it depends on a problem with the product and cooling-off does not.
a.clue: Think about when it starts and what the buyer can do.

b.q: Jarrah in Darwin signs a contract at his front door with a door-to-door seller. That night he decides he does not want it. What is true about his situation?
opts: A cooling-off period may let him cancel without a reason
He can cancel only if the product turns out to be faulty
He cannot cancel, because he already signed the contract
He can cancel only if the seller agrees to it afterwards
b.why: Door-to-door sales are a type of sale that can have a cooling-off period, so Jarrah may cancel without giving a reason. Signing does not remove that right, because the period starts after signing.
b.clue: The period starts after the contract is signed.

a.best: Time after signing in which a buyer can cancel a contract

b.best: A cooling-off period may let him cancel without a reason

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'). The three distractors are all absolutes ('cannot', 'only if', 'only if'), so a student could pick the answer from its wording alone.

'Within a few days' is more definite than the card's 'often a matter of days' and 'depends on the type of sale'. For door-to-door (unsolicited) sales in Australia the period is 10 business days, about two weeks, so 'a few days' could lead students to think they have less time than they do.
